title: pair_word's docstring and querylog.md give an example the one-candidate rule does not pair
goal: Found by the fresh-context review of SP-matmvkn6, item ST-dsre52lb (learn pairs a rules miss's key word only with the one candidate word of the quoted line): the worked example 'unsaved and land: uncommitted changes give uncommitted' in pair_word's docstring (_tools/ql_learn.py) and kb/_self/querylog.md's learn paragraph leaves out that land must be in the question; with a question of only 'unsaved changes' the line has two candidates (land, uncommitted) and gives no pair. The example names the question it assumes, so it agrees with what pair_word returns.

run: import re,sys;sys.path.insert(0,"_tools");import ql_learn as l;q=open("kb/_self/querylog.md",encoding="utf-8").read();d=bool(re.search(r"asked about[^:\x60]*\bland\b",l.pair_word.__doc__));k=bool(re.search(r"\x60pair_word\x60:[^)]*asked[^)]*\bland\b",q));print("example names land in its question: docstring",d,"querylog.md",k);sys.exit(0 if d and k and l.pair_word("unsaved","land: uncommitted changes","land unsaved changes")=="uncommitted" and l.pair_word("unsaved","land: uncommitted changes","unsaved changes") is None else 1)

notes: Planned at the 2026-10-10 whole-backlog triage, which the operator asked to end with every draft planned into a sprint or dropped (sprint 13 of 13, "Orchestration features: ops rows, goal clause map, rescope, query log apply"); it blocks no fitness test and no real user reported it, so it sits in a late sprint of the sequence. Premise: pair_word('unsaved', 'land: uncommitted changes', 'unsaved changes') is None, so the docstring's and querylog.md's example is wrong as worded (2026-10-10: reproduces; land is a second candidate). The check reads the example's parenthesis: asked about ... land ... in the docstring, and 'asked ... land' inside the (`pair_word`: ...) parenthesis of querylog.md's learn paragraph; with the question 'land unsaved changes' the pair is uncommitted. The old pinning check (the one-candidate rule gives no pair for the two-word question) is its last assertion.
